description: lower_guard_boolean (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs:3440) skips its boolean test only when ctx.value_types proves the operand a boolean. The result of a guard comparison (and of not/and/or) has no type recorded there, so every operand of and/or/not in a guard is tested with two Identical ops against true and false, each a call to fz_value_eq_raw_const. For 'c >= 32 and c < 128 and c != 34 and c != 92' that is up to about 12 runtime calls per evaluation; the comparisons themselves are plain icmp. Seen as fz_value_eq_raw_const at 8% of a decode profile (scratchpad b183-6/new.sample summary) and in the CLIF of a scan function. Goal: record bool for the results of guard comparisons, type tests, not, and, or, so the test is emitted only for an operand that can be a non-boolean. Effect size not yet measured in isolation: measure a guarded walk before and after (runtime calls per step, time). Interp is unaffected (native lowering only); check whether the interpreter has the same redundancy.

comments.text: PR #726 (branch fz-sc8.198/guard-booleans). Measured, release build, instructions per byte, develop 394fa1313 -> change: guarded byte walk 604 -> 196; with a non-tail leaf call 787 -> 379; three clauses repeating the guard 1,411 -> 243. No runtime call remains in a guard built from comparisons. Interp unaffected (native lowering only).

title: A guard comparison's result is known to be a boolean
